cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Outside the Scope
cards.instruction: Redirect personal or dangerous questions by declaring them irrelevant, premature, or assigned to another process.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Whether I broke the window is outside this repair meeting's scope.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then let's hold a responsibility meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. After the repairs. We need a safe venue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Location changes require a separate planning discussion.

mechanism: A assumes final jurisdiction over what this interaction may discuss, placing a threatening personal question into another meeting or prior procedural requirement.
confusable: D181 diffuses blame among process stages; D182 evades the question itself by declaring its discussion out of scope or premature.
comparison: Window responsibility is deferred through venue planning; anniversary explanation is deferred through booking and dessert cancellation.
seedUse: All four canonical seeds read. Preserve B practical solutions that A turns into new scope boundaries; authority must govern the conversation itself.
